solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Barb piercing fish soon causing bad suffering (7,6)

indicators.note: the barb goes through the fish, so STING sits inside COD

blocks.note: a barb or sting, as in a pointed remark
early = soon, before the expected time

annotation.surface: An angler describes a nasty accident: a hook through a fish that soon leaves someone in pain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Barb' looks like a fishing hook to go with the fish, but here it is a cutting remark, a sting.
annotation.definitionFit: Something costing dearly causes serious loss or pain to the one who pays.

entries.clue: Sounding harsh about policeman I’m surprised turned back on good judgment (11)

indicators.note: OH is turned round to read HO

annotation.surface: A startled speaker turns their back on good sense when a policeman appears.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nous' is everyday British slang for practical good sense. 'On' simply means 'placed next to' in this down clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Cacophonous describes a harsh, discordant sound.

entries.clue: Move beam, changing article for ironwork, primarily (5)

indicators.note: tells you to swap one letter of SHAFT for another
marks what the article is exchanged for
takes just the first letter of 'ironwork'

blocks.note: a shaft of light is a beam
first letter of ironwork, put in where A was

annotation.surface: An instruction on a building site: move the beam and swap one fitting for some ironwork.
annotation.walkthrough: The builder's picture makes 'beam' a girder, but it is a shaft of light.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to shift a thing is to change its position.

entries.clue: Unproblematic having no kids (9)

blocks.note: issue is the legal word for offspring

annotation.surface: A remark that life without children is easy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Issue' in the sense of children is the old legal term, as in 'died without issue'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses of 'issue', problems and offspring, can be absent.

entries.clue: Cups turned up in hostel bogs (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, read the letters from bottom to top
the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'hostel' into 'bogs'; read them upward

annotation.surface: Someone finds drinking cups in the toilets of a hostel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bogs' is British slang for toilets, which makes the surface nicely grubby.
annotation.definitionFit: Goblets are drinking cups, usually stemmed.

entries.clue: Potty revolutionary cycling for some time (5)

indicators.note: a cycle goes round and round, so the letters rotate and the last comes back to the front

blocks.note: a po is a chamber pot

annotation.surface: A mad rebel takes up cycling for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Potty' reads as crazy but is the noun: a po is a chamber pot, the British nursery word.
annotation.definitionFit: An era or long stretch of history, which 'some time' loosely covers.

entries.clue: Sailor bitten by insect is slowing (9)

indicators.note: the insect's jaws close round the sailor, so TAR goes inside RED ANT

annotation.surface: A seaman stung by an insect finds himself slowing down.
annotation.walkthrough: The insect has to be a specific kind, the red ant, to split round TAR.
annotation.definitionFit: A retardant substance slows a process, such as a fire.

entries.clue: Desire bread from abroad (3)

blocks.note: bread is slang for money, so a foreign currency: Japan's

annotation.surface: A craving for foreign bread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, so foreign bread is a foreign currency.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: a craving, and the currency of Japan.

entries.clue: Each maid peeled fruit (4)

indicators.note: each word loses its outside letters, like skin from fruit

blocks.note: EACH without its first and last letters
MAID without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Each maid peels fruit in the kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peeled' sits naturally with fruit but works on both preceding words.
annotation.definitionFit: Acai is the berry of a South American palm.

entries.clue: Source of virus overlooked in otherwise unobtrusive section of code (10)

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter
the V is left out of the next word
the remaining letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A programmer's warning: the virus was missed, hidden in an innocent-looking piece of code.
annotation.walkthrough: The computing surface is seamless; 'section of code' is the plain definition at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A subroutine is a self-contained section of a program.

entries.clue: Rush imbibing the French wine (8)

indicators.note: SPATE drinks in LES, holding it inside

blocks.note: a spate is a rush or flood

annotation.surface: Someone hastily gulps down the French wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like a verb for hurried drinking, but it is the noun spate.
annotation.definitionFit: Spätlese is a German late-harvest wine.

entries.clue: Listen briefly, political party is short of funds (4-2)

indicators.note: HARK is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

annotation.surface: A plea for attention: a political party has run out of money.
annotation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Irish party, a regular in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal British phrase for someone struggling for cash.

entries.clue: Damage one covered in plastered neutral colour (11)

indicators.note: MAR and I go inside the rearranged letters
drunk, so NEUTRAL is jumbled

annotation.surface: Harm done when someone is splattered with plaster in a beige shade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' suggests plasterwork to match 'neutral colour', but it means drunk. The definition is the last word; 'neutral' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a deep blue pigment, first ground from lapis lazuli brought from 'beyond the sea'.

entries.clue: Crowded company moved to let one go (10)

indicators.note: I, one, is released from IMPRESSED

blocks.note: moved emotionally, impressed; without I it is MPRESSED

annotation.surface: A packed firm is persuaded to lay off a staff member.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moved' reads as relocated, but it means touched emotionally.
annotation.definitionFit: Compressed things are squeezed together, crowded.

entries.clue: Each year small group nakedly abuse nationalist (9)

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters, STICK becomes TIC

blocks.note: a trio is a group of three
to give stick is to criticise; stripped to TIC

annotation.surface: An annual gathering of a few people who strip off and hurl abuse at a nationalist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stick' in the sense of abuse or harsh criticism is British idiom ('take a lot of stick').
annotation.definitionFit: Here nationalist is the adjective: devoted to one's country.

entries.clue: Not scared to go round city (9)

indicators.note: the letters turn about into a new order

annotation.surface: A brave traveller willing to tour a city.
annotation.walkthrough: Doncaster is a town, now a city, in South Yorkshire, England.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this South Yorkshire town was granted city status in 2022.

entries.clue: Popular type not completely creative (4)

indicators.note: only part of the words is used

annotation.surface: A description of a sociable sort who is only half artistic.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the two words, POPUL|AR TY|PE.
annotation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone showily creative.

entries.clue: Cry over piquant wraps (4)

indicators.note: to wrap something is to enclose it, so the word for piquant closes round the letter for over

annotation.surface: Someone weeps over spicy wraps at a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wraps' looks like food to go with piquant, but it is the container verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an owl's call or a burst of laughter, both kinds of cry.

entries.clue: Dreadful thing stopping witness attending since (6,4)

indicators.note: THING is mangled into INGTH
INGTH plugs the gap between SEE and AT

annotation.surface: Something awful prevented a witness from coming to court.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition hides as the last word, a humble conjunction.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Seeing that' and 'since' both mean 'because'.

entries.clue: One charming rogue in Crete (7)

indicators.note: something gone rogue has broken from its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A charming rogue on holiday in Crete.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One charming rogue' reads as a unit, but 'rogue' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: An enticer charms or lures others.

entries.clue: Perceives sixth sense that is singular (6)

annotation.surface: A remark that someone's sixth sense is unique.
annotation.walkthrough: Every piece is a standard abbreviation strung in clue order.
annotation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, perceive.

entries.clue: Stop exhausted outside shelter to rest (5)

indicators.note: STOP emptied of its middle leaves SP
the emptied word sits on the outside, its two letters flanking the shelter

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side

annotation.surface: A worn-out walker halts beside a shelter to rest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stop exhausted' reads as someone too tired to go on, but 'exhausted' empties the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sleep is the fullest kind of rest.

entries.clue: Transport returned in the westbound lane of airway (8)

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the letters read in reverse
the reversed transport is placed inside 'the'
in an across clue, going west is right to left, so LA becomes AL

annotation.surface: A car is seen driving the wrong way on a westbound lane.
annotation.walkthrough: The motoring surface hides a medical definition at the end: 'of airway' needs an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Tracheal means relating to the trachea, the windpipe or airway.

entries.clue: Treasure group of nomads picked up (5)

indicators.note: heard, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: a horde is a nomadic tribe or throng

annotation.surface: A band of wanderers comes across a treasure trove.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' pretends the nomads collected the treasure.
annotation.definitionFit: As a noun, treasure can mean a stockpile of valuables, which is exactly this.

entries.clue: Do exploit male recruits regularly (7,3)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken

annotation.surface: An order to take advantage of the men being enlisted from time to time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the verb, but it is the noun, a hairdo.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Do' is informal shorthand for hairdo; this layered style was popular in the 1970s.

entries.clue: Blunder is end for white bishop (3)

indicators.note: only the last letter of 'white' is used

blocks.note: Rt Rev, Right Reverend, a bishop's title

annotation.surface: A chess comment: losing the white bishop is a mistake that ends the game.
annotation.walkthrough: The chess picture is false: the bishop is a churchman, RR being the Right Reverend.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to make a mistake.

entries.clue: Keen to help five dons (4)

indicators.note: AID puts on V like a garment, wrapping it

annotation.surface: Five university lecturers are eager to lend a hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like Oxbridge teachers, but it is the verb, puts on.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean eager and enthusiastic.

entries.clue: Bird to shake crest on overturned snare (4,9)

indicators.note: TRAP turned over reads PART
in an across clue, RIDGE comes after PART

blocks.note: the crest of a hill is a ridge

annotation.surface: A bird ruffles its crest over an upturned trap.
annotation.walkthrough: The crest reads as feathers, but it is the top of a hill.
annotation.definitionFit: The rock partridge is a game bird of southern Europe.
